1.explanation:
• tree/index.md & index.en-us.md: document the Tree API, props and expected data shapes (including the `key` and `data` props) so you know how Tree is supposed to consume user data.  
• tree/adaptor/index.jsx: contains the adaptor logic that wraps or clones incoming data, and is the first step that leads into the `drill` routine where `pos` is computed and assigned.  
• tree/demo/basic.md & demo/data.md: show canonical examples of passing plain JS objects as treeData; reviewing these helps reproduce the bug by supplying similarly structured (but frozen) objects.  
• tree/demo/virtual-tree.md: demonstrates a use-case that relies on the internal `pos` property for virtualization—this will fail in the same way and is a minimal reproduction for the frozen-object error.
1.bug_scenario: Upgrading the Tree component from 1.19.x to 1.20.23 triggers “TypeError: Cannot add property pos, object is not extensible.” In the provided screenshots you can see the failure happens inside the internal `drill` function (next/es/tree/view/tree.js:159), where `item.pos` is logged as `undefined` and then `item.pos = pos` is executed on an object that has been frozen or sealed by the user’s immutable data. The console error and call stack pinpoint the assignment of `pos` on a non-extensible node object as the root cause.
